novel.title: QA Sample: The Glass Meridian (test data)

pieces.text: The tide came in grey over Port Calder, and Ilse read it in the window glass before it reached the harbour wall.
Wren asked her what she saw. She said rain, and a ledger, and a man who would want it back.
Somewhere above the town, in the guild house, her old teacher was waiting for an answer she had not given.
Corin pressed the guild mark into the warm glass and handed it to her without a word.
The burn on his wrist was older than she was. She had asked about it once, as a child, and he had looked at the hills and said nothing at all.
Ilse took the mark. From that night she was one of the Glasswrights, whatever came after.
The Archive smelled of dust and lamp oil. Tamsin had the door open before Ilse finished reading the lock.
The Ledger of Tides was lighter than either of them had thought. They argued about who would carry it, and then ran.
Across the square, Magistrate Hale counted the raised hands in Council Hall and smiled at the number.
He did not yet know the Archive stood open.
They left Port Calder by the salt road before dawn. Tamsin walked ahead; Ilse carried the ledger.
By the third night they had stopped arguing. By the fourth they were friends, though neither said it.

pieces.text: The bell rang once. Twice, then.
Mira woke before the bells.
The road north was empty.
Mira and Kai crossed at dawn.
Kai said nothing. Miracles were rare.
Pell waited in the tower.
Ash fell over everything. Mira, Kai and Pell.
Home, at last.

Mira drew the Sunblade and raised it high.
Orrin was nineteen years old, and his hands were steady.
Her grey eyes shone with tears. Mira wept.
They travelled for two days to reach Saltport from Greykeep.
Interlude
Orrin gripped the Sunblade with both hands.
Mira smiled at the guard.
They spoke of Mira often, and of the Sunblade.
The Heiress said nothing.
Deep underground, the caves were cold.
Kai cast the fire spell anyway, half an hour later.
The Sunblade lay forgotten.
Orrin drew the Sunblade, the blade in his hand.
Pell, 23, laughed.
Alex’s hair was black as night.
Mira returned, said nothing, and walked on.
It took a week to reach Saltport from Greykeep.
